claims.statement: From 18 February 2027, LMT batteries, industrial batteries above the stated capacity and EV batteries require an electronic battery passport accessible through a QR code.
The Batteries Regulation takes a lifecycle approach and the passport is intended to provide value-chain information, supporting a lifecycle rather than one-time document product.

contrary_evidence: Large OEMs and standards consortia are building passport infrastructure, while compliance alone may become an interoperable commodity.

risks: Telemetry rights and security are difficult.
Residual-value predictions create reliance and product-liability exposure if presented as guarantees.

structure.commercial_archetype: serialised asset provenance and residual-value registry
structure.control_point: battery QR-passport issuance and second-life ownership transfer
structure.critical_dependency: OEM-authorised BMS telemetry, materials provenance and independent condition-test rights

thesis: Issue standards-aligned battery passports for industrial and light-mobility battery integrators, then preserve consented usage, repair and state-of-health evidence through resale into second life. Passport compliance is the wedge; proprietary degradation-to-resale outcome curves become the durable underwriting asset.
title: Battery Passport Residual-Value Registry
